answer: Randomized Identity Inlet Assignment: each new agent identity is admitted only through a randomly drawn inlet slot, seeded by a public beacon the attacker cannot precompute. At the violet vertex of each epoch, slots are reshuffled and assigned to verified submissions. An attacker cannot predict which inlet their clones receive, so flooding requires committing real work to every slot before the seed is revealed. Clones landing in already-filled inlets are discarded, forcing a per-identity cost of one full submission cycle per attempt.
